units.translation: I have restored ἀκλαγγείς [not barking], which, since in older manuscripts it was written ἀκλαγεῖς [not barking], as many forms of the verb κλαγγάνω [to bark] and words derived from it are often written with a single γ [gamma], was changed by scribes, who did not consider that dogs are said not to cry out but to bark, into ἀκραγείς [not barking], which is now read in M. By the same error κύνες κεκραγυῖαι [dogs barking], arising from κεκλαγυίαι [having barked], is written in most manuscripts of Xenophon's Cynegeticus 3, 9 and 6, 27 instead of κεκλαγγυται [they have barked], which is preserved in others. In Choephori 535, where the manuscript has κέκλαγεν [he has barked], H. L. Ahrens wrote κέκλαγγεν [he has barked], Robortellus κέκραγεν [he has cried out]. Aeschylus called the dogs ἀκλαγγείς [not barking] to distinguish dogs used metaphorically from dogs in the proper sense: a form of speech quite common among the tragedians. With the alpha privative before a mute with a liquid lengthened, compare ἄτρυτον πόδα [unwearied foot] in a trimeter of Aeschylus Eum. 403, and άτρωτος [unwounded] in a trimeter of Eubulus in Athenaeus 9 p. 4491: ἓν ὄνομα πολλοῖς· τρωτός ἄτρωτος, δασύς [one name for many: vulnerable, invulnerable, hairy]. The Grypes are compared with dogs because they are guardians of gold: just as Aeschylus called a woman who guards the house in her husband's absence γυναῖκα πιστὴν — δωμάτων κύνα [a faithful woman — a dog of the house] in Agam. v. 607. The adjective ἀκραγής [not barking], compounded from ἄκρος [highest] and ἄγος [curse], is nowhere read except in certain glosses of grammarians.
For guard against the sharp-mouthed, not barking dogs of Zeus, the griffins.
one name for many: vulnerable, invulnerable, hairy
a faithful woman — a dog of the house
The old Attic spelling ἄκλαυτος [unwept], of which rare examples remain in the manuscripts of the tragedians, I have restored in both places for ἀκλαύτοις [unwept] and άκλαυστος [unwept].

[Introduced from a gloss Eum. 352 παλλεύκων δὲ πέπλων ἄμοιρος ἄκληρος ἐτύχθην [I was made without share or lot in the all-white robes], where, as sense and meter demand, I wrote παλλεύκων δὲ πέπλων ἄμοιρος μούνα ἐτύχθην [I was made alone without share in the all-white robes]: about which I spoke in the Preface to the fifth Leipzig edition p. CI.]
I was made without share or lot in the all-white robes,
I was made alone without share in the all-white robes:
An uninvited guest, creeping all day long.
I have come not uninvited, but summoned.
to be in full bloom, to be at the right time
Intransitive ἀκμάζει [it is the right time] means it is time, it is necessary.
It is time to cling to the images.
For now it is time for deceitful Persuasion to descend.
in the prime of life, youthful
the one still lacking in youthful prime.
as many as were in their prime by nature.
having yoked this chariot to horses in their prime.
And it was no longer the moment to delay.
It is the moment not to delay.
I bring down the heavy-falling force of my foot.
Tear the folded robe with the force of your hands.
